text:
maria: Quick follow-up on the locality-binding handshake we prototyped yesterday — hit an edge case where CP affinity flips during AZ failover and the tenant traffic lands on a relay with stale route bindings.
jonathan: Which step in the handshake is failing — the token exchange or the post-attach route sync?
sahil: Saw this too. Happens when the attach completes but the agent's local route cache hasn't refreshed before new requests arrive.
maria: Right — attach succeeds, agent writes a local mapping, then a brief network flap causes the controlplane to reassign affinity. Agent still uses old local mapping for ~30s.
arjun: Is this the previously-discussed STALE_BINDING window? We had a 60s TTL in the prototype to avoid thrash.
maria: In the prototype it was 60s, but we observed a 30s window in practice where frontend retries exacerbate the problem (requests route to a CP/edge that no longer owns that tenant).
jonathan: Two quick options: (A) shorten binding TTL + stricter atomic swap (risk: more churn), (B) keep TTL but make agent perform a pre-request binding check (risk: extra latency on steady path).
sahil: Agree. Also consider a pragmatic fallback: on detect of bind-mismatch, agent should fail-fast to the regional-relay rather than attempt blind retries that hit authz errors. That preserves tail latency.
maria: Proposed hybrid: keep TTL=60s, but add lightweight probe on first request after attach that validates route ownership (one controlplane handshake RPC, cheap). If mismatch -> immediate rebind or fallback to regional-relay.
arjun: Sounds reasonable. Implementation concerns: we need that probe to be idempotent and not increase CP load too much. Could piggyback on existing heartbeat stream from agent to CP.
jonathan: Exactly — piggyback on heartbeat. Heartbeat already sends last-known-binding; add a binding-version header and CP can reply with 'owned|steal|unknown'. Agent acts accordingly.
sahil: We should enumerate failure handling states: 
- owned -> proceed
- steal -> rebind, refresh local route cache, mark metric cp.binding.steal
- unknown -> fallback to regional-relay and schedule backoff rebind attempt
maria: Also need to consider cross-account peering cutovers where IP preservation matters. If we fall back to relays frequently during cutover, customers with source-ip expectations will see diff behavior. We must surface the fallback in Console and in metrics.
arjun: Yep. Add a per-tenant telemetry flag: last_fallback_reason and last_binding_epoch for debug. Expose via Redwood Console as a small timeline.
jonathan: One more tradeoff: token exchange vs short-lived certs. If we rely on token exchange for quick rebinds, we avoid heavy cert churn but must secure the transport for token issuance. If we go cert-first, rebinds are slower but simpler auth path.
sahil: Token exchange seems better for fast rebinds. Suggest we implement a two-step: token pre-issue at attach time (one-time short-lived token stored in agent) + on-demand ephemeral cert issuance when binding changes. This minimizes latency while keeping auditable cert rotations.
maria: Good. For rollout: implement probe + heartbeat binding-version check in agent, token pre-issue in controlplane, regional-relay fallback path. Start with a canary for 5% of onboardings.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: infra/cp-binding-probe v0.1 -> target: staging -> ETA 10m :rocket:
jonathan: After canary, we should run a synthetic test that simulates AZ failover and confirms no >1% increase in P50 and no user-facing auth errors.
arjun: I'll own the synthetic and dashboards. Will add cp.binding.* metrics and a small dashboard card for Console.
sahil: I'll add unit tests for heartbeat piggyback and a small e2e that reproduces the stale-binding flow.
maria: I'll draft a short RFC addendum with the hybrid approach and risk table. Keep notes for oncall playbook: how to detect repeated fallbacks (alert if >5 fallbacks/min for a tenant).
jonathan: Thanks. One last note — consider marking the rebind decision as a semantically observable event (trace context) so traces show fallbacks. Would help debugging cross-service.
maria: Agreed. I'll include trace/span semantic in the RFC. OK, breaking to tasks: arjun -> dashboards/tests, sahil -> agent probe/tests, jonathan -> CP token flow, maria -> RFC + rollout plan.
arjun: ack.
sahil: ack.
jonathan: ack.
deploy-bot: canary started: infra/cp-binding-probe v0.1 -> staging (1/1) :white_check_mark:
